clue.text: Method of torturing those serving General Tom?

parts.note: General Tom Thumb was the tiny showman of P T Barnum's circus; the possessive gives his name plus S
a crew is the people who serve aboard a ship or under a captain

explanation.surface: A grim question about how the servants of a famous little general were tormented.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the clue as the crew belonging to Tom Thumb: THUMB'S CREW, run together as one word.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a medieval device for crushing the digits, used as an instrument of torture.

clue.text: Court case involving evidence of accident relating to fork

indicators.note: a case involving something holds it inside, so one word wraps the other

parts.note: a trial is a case heard in court
a dent in a car is the visible sign of a bump

explanation.surface: A lawsuit hinges on proof of a crash involving some cutlery.
explanation.definitionFit: A trident is a three-pronged fork, so the adjective describes something with that shape.

clue.text: Absolute fool, losing head

indicators.note: losing its head means the word for fool drops its first letter

parts.note: a nutter is a slang word for a crazy person or idiot

explanation.surface: An insult: someone is a complete idiot who has lost their head.
explanation.definitionFit: Utter and absolute are synonyms meaning complete, as in utter nonsense.

clue.text: Predatory behaviour's infectious after time in prison

indicators.note: one piece comes after the other, so the prison term is placed first

parts.note: bird is British slang for a prison sentence, from rhyming slang 'bird-lime' for time
a catching disease is one that spreads easily

explanation.surface: Someone's predatory conduct is said to have spread like a disease after a spell inside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bird' meaning a jail term is British slang (rhyming slang: bird-lime = time). The 's of 'behaviour's' stands for 'is', a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Hunting and seizing birds is the predatory activity of hawks, cats and fowlers.

clue.text: Work at eating cold cut

parts.note: C is the standard abbreviation for cold, as on a tap
to hew is to cut with blows of an axe

explanation.surface: Someone works at a meal of cold cuts.
explanation.definitionFit: Chewing is the jaw's work when munching food.

clue.text: Great pleasure accepting working Government's extension

indicators.note: a word accepting others takes them inside itself

parts.note: elation is great joy
a machine that is on is working
G is a common abbreviation for government

explanation.surface: Delight that the working government has been granted more time.
explanation.definitionFit: A lengthening or stretching out is an extension.

clue.text: Politicians without conviction back in a difficult situation

indicators.note: back here tells us to read the politicians word from right to left

parts.note: wets was Thatcher's term for moderate Conservatives lacking resolve

explanation.surface: Feeble politicians are once more in trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wets' is British political slang, Margaret Thatcher's label for the soft-line Tories in her cabinet.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in a stew is to be in a state of worry or a fix.

clue.text: Various tours use a particular set of clothes

indicators.note: various suggests the letters take a different arrangement

explanation.surface: Different holidays call for a particular wardrobe.
explanation.definitionFit: A bride's outfit of clothes and linen gathered for marriage is her trousseau.

clue.text: One fitted in to join handle

indicators.note: fitted in signals one piece placed inside another

parts.note: to weld is to join metal by heat
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A piece is fitted to join a handle.
explanation.definitionFit: To wield a tool is to handle it skilfully.

clue.text: Protein, one distributed for tenner

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: distributed means the letters are spread about into a new order

explanation.surface: A protein is handed out at one per ten-pound note.
explanation.walkthrough: A tenner is a British ten-pound note; 'distributed' rearranges FOR TENNER into NTERFERON after I.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a signalling protein released by cells to fight viruses.

clue.text: Geometric shape featured in first chapter?

parts.note: the first is number one

explanation.surface: A shape appears in the opening chapter of a book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First chapter' reads as chapter one: C followed by ONE.
explanation.definitionFit: A solid tapering from a circular base to a point is a basic geometric figure.

clue.text: He wrote nonsense for diversion of aircrews in lounge

indicators.note: in places the rearranged letters inside the lounging word

parts.note: to loll is to lounge lazily

indicators.note: a diversion moves things off their course, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An author's comic writing entertains aircrew lounging between flights.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Diversion of' signals the anagram of the eight aircrew letters, which sits inside the lounging word after its first letter; 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The author of the Alice books is the classic writer of nonsense verse such as 'Jabberwocky'.

clue.text: Add value to note carried by German?

indicators.note: a thing carried by someone sits inside them

parts.note: Erich is a typical German man's name

explanation.surface: A German carries a banknote to make himself richer.
explanation.definitionFit: To improve the worth or quality of something is to make it richer.

clue.text: Noise from visitor should be anticipated

indicators.note: noise from signals the sound of the words, not their spelling

parts.note: a visitor is a guest, and should is shortened to 'd, giving guest'd

explanation.surface: The sound of a guest arriving should have been expected.
explanation.walkthrough: Say GUEST'D (guest + 'd for 'should') and it sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To have predicted or supposed something is to have anticipated it.

clue.text: Flirty Scot quite upset hearts

indicators.note: upset signals that the letters are knocked into a new order

parts.note: H is the card-playing abbreviation for hearts

explanation.surface: A flirtatious Scotsman quite upsets hearts.
explanation.definitionFit: Coy and playfully teasing behaviour toward admirers is flirtatious.

clue.text: Reliability in ending of incipient decay wins others round

indicators.note: the ending of a word is its last letter

parts.note: rust is the decay of iron

indicators.note: round signals the letters turned about into a new order

explanation.surface: Dependability lies in rot nipped in the bud, with others won over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reliability in' is definition plus link; 'round' looks like a container signal but rearranges WINS OTHERS, placed after the last letter of 'incipient' and the decay word.
explanation.definitionFit: Being dependable and worthy of confidence is the meaning of reliability.

clue.text: 6A remarkable thing turned up, transformed into a wailing noise

indicators.note: turned up in a down clue means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a lulu is an outstanding or remarkable example of something

indicators.note: transformed means the following letters change into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Something remarkable shows up and turns into a howl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turned up' reverses LULU to ULUL; 'transformed' rearranges INTO A to give ATION.
explanation.definitionFit: A high-pitched howl or keening cry of grief is a wailing sound.

clue.text: Demonstrated essential part of better fabric

parts.note: protesters who staged a sit-in sat in, so demonstrated gives sat in

indicators.note: the essential part is the core, so take the middle letters of the word

explanation.surface: A demonstration of the essence of a better fabric.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Demonstrated' is SAT IN, as protesters do in a sit-in; the middle of bETTEr is ETTE.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a cotton or mixed cloth imitating satin, so it is a textile.

clue.text: Pooh-pooh what the King's jester makes him do while travelling?

definitions.meaning: to dismiss something as too ridiculous to consider

definitions.text: what the King's jester makes him do while travelling?
definitions.meaning: a jester's job is to make the king laugh, and when the king travels he is away from his court

explanation.surface: A court fool keeps the monarch amused on his journeys.
explanation.definitionFit: Dismissing something with ridicule is the idiom's sense; literally it describes making a monarch chuckle when away from the palace.

clue.text: Police search -a tedious thing when linked to connected computers

parts.note: a drag is something boring
a net or network is a set of linked computers

explanation.surface: A dull police hunt is linked to computer networks.
explanation.definitionFit: A systematic sweep to catch criminals, like a fishing net trawled through an area.

clue.text: Act, but waveringly, expressing suspicion

parts.note: to do is to act

indicators.note: something done waveringly is unsteady, so the letters move about

explanation.surface: Someone acts hesitantly, showing mistrust.
explanation.definitionFit: Uncertainty or mistrust about something is a suspicion.

clue.text: Inoperative gun's working internally

indicators.note: internally means placed inside the gun word

parts.note: the Bren is a British light machine gun
OK means functioning or working

explanation.surface: A gun that should be working internally is out of action.
explanation.walkthrough: The Bren was the standard British army light machine gun; the 's of 'gun's' stands for 'is', a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A machine that does not work is out of order, not functioning.

clue.text: Anger recalled after this country's imported dagger

indicators.note: imported means brought in, so one piece goes inside the other
recalled means called back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: to irk is to annoy or anger
for a British paper, this country is the UK

explanation.surface: Anger at a dagger brought into the country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Recalled' turns the anger word round to KRI, and 'imported' brings the country inside it after the first letter; 'after' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the curved knife of the Gurkha soldiers of Nepal, a kind of dagger.

clue.text: Second bundle of equipment one takes off

parts.note: a kit is a set of tools or gear

explanation.surface: A second kit bag for someone setting off.
explanation.definitionFit: A comic sketch that mimics or parodies its subject takes it off.

clue.text: One invested in munitions

indicators.note: invested in means wrapped inside, so the answer is found within the word

explanation.surface: Someone invests in arms.
explanation.definitionFit: A single thing or the number one is a unit.

clue.text: One takes the best aim at snooker

parts.note: the pick of the bunch is the best
in snooker, the player aims to get balls into a pocket

explanation.surface: A snooker player lines up their best shot at the pocket.
explanation.walkthrough: Snooker is a cue game, popular in Britain, where balls are potted into the table's pockets.
explanation.definitionFit: A thief who steals from people's pockets is someone who takes.

clue.text: Style, fashion, the ultimate in elegance

parts.note: ton is an old word for fashion, from French bon ton

indicators.note: the ultimate means the last, so take the final letter

explanation.surface: Style and fashion are the last word in elegance.
explanation.definitionFit: The general character or manner of something is its style.

clue.text: Mistress dancing in lace, concealing loathing

indicators.note: concealing means holding hidden inside
dancing means the letters move about into a new order

parts.note: hate means loathing

explanation.surface: The lady of the house dances in lace, hiding her hatred.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dancing' rearranges IN LACE into CLAINE, and that wraps HATE after its C.
explanation.definitionFit: The woman in charge of a large house or castle is its mistress.
